story: At 5:17 on a sunny Saturday in Sumter Oaks, Gary and Donna are cheerfully practicing their third-shot drops at the Rec Center, with Donna urging Gary to grab a paddle before the 6 o'clock parade. Hal is out on Magnolia Loop with a resolute stride, while Rosa, content in her kitchen, is setting bagged Halloween treats by the door. Up and down the street, grandkids in costumes, orange-trimmed golf carts, and ringing doorbells are signaling that the evening's festivities are about to begin.
events: Town news: Trick-or-treaters are out on Magnolia Loop: visiting grandkids in costumes, golf carts trimmed in orange, and doorbells ringing up and down the street.
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Grab the bagged Halloween treats and set them by the door for the parade

gary.thought_process: Donna just walked up while I'm still on court one with the two hours Hal's been watching the clock on. It's 5:17 and the parade is at 6, so I can't spend much longer here. I've gotten my third-shot drops in, so the polite thing is to greet her, tell her the drills helped, and let her know I need to wrap up soon to get my cart ready and head to the Loop. Rosa's hot cider invitation is worth passing along too, since she asked me to tell them.

parameters.content: Donna, good timing. Those third-shot drops are finally landing soft, thanks to you. I've got to wrap up soon for the 6 o'clock parade, but Rosa says there's hot cider on her porch afterward for you and Hal.

donna.thought_process: I just got to the Rec Center and Gary's right here in line-of-sight. I already offered him a two-hour court this week back at tick 211, so I shouldn't repeat that pitch. The flamingo business with Hal is settled, and the parade is at 6, only about forty minutes off. Best move is to use this moment: get Gary on the court for a quick drill of those third-shot drops, then head to the parade. A short, cheerful line moves things forward without re-asking what I already asked.

parameters.content: There's my partner! We've got maybe half an hour before the parade, so grab a paddle and let's get a few of those third-shot drops in. Then we'll go roll that cart out in style.

hal.thought_process: Donna's flamingos are squared away, so that item is off my list. Gary's cart is the one violation I haven't settled, and he's heading for the Rec Center. The parade is at 6 and it's 5:17, so there's time to look him over before the cart comes out. But I've watched him and Donna drill third-shot drops, and I know I'm half-looking for an excuse to go easy on the man. I'll go find Gary and have a straight talk about L-01 rather than lurk with my binoculars.

parameters.content: Heading to the Rec Center to find Gary and settle the question of his cart modifications before the parade rolls at six.

rosa.thought_process: I'm back home at Rosa's House with no one else around, and it's 5:17 PM on Halloween. The welcome dinner is done and everyone left happy. My treats are bagged and my evening is clear for the parade at the Loop with Gary and Donna. The kitchen is the useful thing here: I should grab the bagged treats so I'm ready to head out to Magnolia Loop. No need to speak to anyone since nobody's in sight.

parameters.content: Grab the bagged Halloween treats and set them by the door for the parade

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
